The image shows a soybean plant with dark green leaves that appear wrinkled, curled, and somewhat small/thick. The plant looks compact/stunted. No obvious leaf spots or lesions. Some lower leaves show slight yellowing.

Top candidates based on symptoms: Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus, Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus, Green_stem_disorder. Let me check references.

Green_stem_disorder doesn't match (shows mature plants with green stems). BPMV shows mottling which I don't see. Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus looks very similar with the dark green, wrinkled, curled leaves. Let me check a few more references.

None of those match well. My initial prediction is **Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus** based on the dark green, wrinkled, curled, small/thick leaves with no obvious spots or lesions.

Now let me check the attractor guide.

Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus is listed as over-predicted (5x wrong). The alternatives are Septoria_brown_spot, Sudden_death_syndrome, Fusarium, Soybean_Cyst_Nematode, and White_Mold. None of these fit the test image:
- No brown spots (rules out Septoria)
- No interveinal chlorosis/necrosis (rules out SDS)
- No wilting or root symptoms (rules out Fusarium)
- No field-pattern yellowing (rules out SCN)
- No white mold growth (rules out White_Mold)

The test image strongly matches Soybean_Dwarf_Mosaic_Virus: dark green, wrinkled, curled, small, thick-looking leaves on a compact plant, which are the hallmark symptoms described in the KB.
